title: Tenant Residency Beacon Scheduler and Evidence Serializer
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a daemon and pipeline that periodically captures cryptographically-signed residency snapshots and tenant isolation evidence for Dedicated capacity customers. The system will schedule per-tenant beacons, collect host and network metadata, serialize evidence packages in multiple signed formats, and publish artifacts to the compliance archive for audits.
background: Customers with Dedicated capacity require deterministic proof that their workloads execute in region X and are isolated from other tenants. Existing ad-hoc scripts produce CSV exports and manual sign-offs; we need a production-grade service to automate generation, signing, retention, and export of residency artifacts aligned with retention policies and KMS signing requirements.
proposal: Build a modular service with three components: (1) Beacon Scheduler (per-tenant cron-like scheduler respecting customer retention policies and jitter windows), (2) Evidence Collector & Normalizer (collects host metadata, container identity, network namespace hashes, volume attachments, kernel provenance, and runtime telemetry), and (3) Evidence Serializer & Signer (packages evidence into JSONL + human-readable summary, signs with project KMS key and optional Sigstore cosign for provenance, and writes artifacts to the compliance S3 bucket and the Console's evidence viewer). Artifacts should support multiple retention tiers and formats (compact JSONL for machine ingestion, PDF summary for auditors, OCI artifact bundle for notarization).
design_notes: Scheduler will support tenant-level configuration: frequency (hourly/daily/weekly), retention tier (30/90/365 days), jitter window to avoid thundering herd, and blackout windows for maintenance
Evidence Collector runs privileged read-only probes (via a secure probe agent) and uses a pluggable adapter pattern for cloud metadata sources (AWS, GCP, Azure) and on-prem node attestations
Normalize network isolation evidence to a canonical signature: list of ENIs/subnets + VPC ID + security group snapshot hashed with canonical ordering
Serializer will produce two canonical artifacts: a machine-consumable manifest.jsonl and a human-readable audit-summary.pdf; both will include SHA256 checksum and KMS signature metadata
Signing flow: primary signing with customer-specific KMS key when available; fallback to Redwood platform signing key; optional cosign/Sigstore entry for public verifiability
Retention enforcement: lifecycle policies on S3 + metadata catalog to automatically purge expired artifacts; deletions must be recorded in an immutable deletion ledger for compliance
Access control: evidence artifacts inherit tenant RBAC; only authorized compliance users and tenant owners can request exports; signed export links will be short-lived and logged
Performance: collector probes must have a <5s tail per host; batching across up to 100 hosts to avoid API quotas
Observability: emit metrics for scheduler drift, collection success rate, signing latency, artifact size, and retention purges
api_contracts: GET /internal/compliance/v1/artifacts/{artifact_id}/download - authenticated signed URL for artifact
POST /internal/compliance/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/config - update tenant beacon and retention config
storage_formats: manifest.jsonl (newline-delimited canonical JSON records, each record type has well-defined schema version)
audit-summary.pdf (renderer produces auditor-friendly summary with diagrams and checksums)
oci-bundle.tar.gz (OCI-compatible artifact layout with cosign signatures and provenance files)
deletion-ledger.log (append-only ledger entries recording artifact purges and the deletion rationale)
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler supports per-tenant frequency and retention settings surfaced through API
A full end-to-end beacon run produces manifest.jsonl + audit-summary.pdf + signed checksums in the compliance S3 bucket
Artifacts are signed with platform or customer KMS keys and include signature metadata consumable by our verifier
Retention purge runs remove expired artifacts and append a signed deletion entry to deletion-ledger.log
Console exposes an evidence viewer tab that lists artifacts, supports preview of audit-summary.pdf, and generates short-lived signed download links
Metrics emitted to monitoring: beacon_runs_total, beacon_failures_total, signing_latency_seconds, artifact_size_bytes, retention_purge_count
Automated tests cover collector adapters (mock cloud metadata), signer (KMS mock), and serializer output validation against JSON schemas
tasks: Design schema for manifest.jsonl and audit-summary PDF (security & legal review)
Implement Beacon Scheduler service with tenant config API and cron engine
Build Collector adapters for AWS/GCP/Azure metadata and on-prem agent
Implement Evidence Serializer, checksumming, and KMS signing integration
Integrate optional Sigstore cosign step and store provenance metadata
Add retention lifecycle manager and deletion ledger writer
Create Console UI for evidence listing, preview, and export
Add observability dashboards and define SLOs for collection and signing
Write unit/integration tests and e2e compliance test harness
Prepare runbook for incident triage and a compliance FAQ for customers
risks: KMS key management complexity for customer-owned keys could delay rollout; mitigation: support platform fallback and documented key onboarding flow
Collector probes require elevated host visibility; mitigation: limit probes to read-only operations and use signed agent binaries + attestation
Large tenants with thousands of hosts could create storage and signing throughput spikes; mitigation: throttle, shard scheduling windows, and incremental artifact diffs
Legal/regulatory review may require additional fields in artifacts per jurisdiction; mitigation: feature flag per-region and extend schema without breaking older versions
